title: Columnwise quasi-isomorphisms induce first-quadrant total quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Let C be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let K and L be first-quadrant double complexes [def-sp-double-complex-total], and let f:K→L be a double-complex morphism. Suppose for every n the map of resolution columns K.flip.X n→L.flip.X n induced by f is a quasi-isomorphism, that is, it induces isomorphisms on every homology object. Then the canonical total map Tot(f):Tot(K)→Tot(L) is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma 12.25.4, finite-diagonal argument, applied to column cones

proof.text: Extend both bicomplexes by zero to integer indices. Take the mapping cone of each column map, with its natural differential in the other direction. Each column cone is acyclic by the column quasi-isomorphism hypothesis. The resolution index is bounded below by -1, and the other index by 0.

source.place: Lemma 12.25.4, finite-diagonal argument, applied to column cones

proof.text: The total of the column-cone bicomplex is isomorphic to the cone of total.map f: both consist degreewise of the finite target diagonal and the shifted finite source diagonal. The cone differential agrees with the total differential after multiplying the shifted source components by the usual degree-dependent signs. Shift the lower bounds to zero and apply the first-quadrant spectral sequence, using the other direction as filtration. Its first page is the homology of the column cones, hence zero. All stable pages are zero. The finite filtration on homology has zero graded pieces; induction from the final zero step proves zero homology. Thus the total cone is acyclic, and the mapping-cone criterion proves total.map f is a quasi-isomorphism.
